newsitem.title: PERU: Video shows Peruvian rebels planning assault.
newsitem.headline: Video shows Peruvian rebels planning assault.

text.p: A video released on Peruvian television early on Saturday showed guerrillas from the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) meticulously planning their dramatic assault on the Japanese ambassador's residence.

The video, sent to Panamericana Television by the rebels, showed a masked guerrilla -- presumed to be the MRTA's leader, Nestor Cerpa Cartolini -- demonstrating a scale model of the compound to fellow rebels armed with automatic rifles, grenades and two-way radios.

It also pictured the guerrillas, their faces half covered with red and white scarves, taking positions in the ambulance some of them used to enter the building in Tuesday night's commando-style attack.
Released hostages confirmed the identities of the guerrillas.
The storming of the residence during a lavish cocktail party late on Tuesday was reportedly directed by Cerpa via cellular telephone from an unknown hideout in Peru.
While a group of guerrillas blew a hole in an outside wall, others entered in the ambulance and another group threw off their disguises as waiters and joined the assault.
The rebels on Saturday were still holding about 340 hostages, including high-ranking diplomats, businessmen and officials.

Anti-terrorism police sources said Cerpa was continuing to direct the siege by radio from somewhere in Lima. Telephone lines and cellular communications to the building have been cut off since Wednesday.
